description: The history table on the audit database: every row change, kept forever.
rationale: The shape the PostgreSQL wiki's audit trigger has used for years, so existing queries mean what they already meant. Unpartitioned on purpose: the store keeps a rolling window and this keeps everything, which is the whole reason the publication has to publish via the partition root -- a change arriving as the ROOT table's is a change this ordinary table can accept. The primary key is (event_id, action_tstamp_tx), matching the publisher's, and that is not cosmetic: the store MUST include the partition key in its key, so a narrower key here would reject rows the publisher considers distinct and stall the subscription with a duplicate-key error that neither side reports as a migration failure.

intents.comment: Row-level history received from the store database.
One row per row change on the publisher. Never rotated.

columns.name: event_id
columns.comment: Monotonic id assigned by the publisher.

columns.name: relid
columns.comment: OID of that table on the publisher.

columns.name: session_user_name
columns.comment: Login role at the time of the change.

columns.name: action_tstamp_tx
columns.comment: Transaction start time. The partition key on the publisher.

columns.name: application_name
columns.comment: application_name of the session that made the change.

columns.name: client_addr
columns.comment: Client address, when there was one.

columns.name: client_port
columns.comment: Client port, when there was one.

columns.name: client_query
columns.comment: The statement that caused the change.

columns.name: row_data
columns.comment: The row before the change, as key/value.

columns.name: changed_fields
columns.comment: Only the columns an UPDATE altered.

columns.name: statement_only
columns.comment: True for a statement-level trigger with no row.
